builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: See the Answer, Learn to Embed: Learning Universal Multimodal Embeddings from Hindsight
summary: HEME replaces inference-time intermediate reasoning in multimodal embedding models with a hindsight-distilled student: a teacher trained with access to the paired candidate (via a hindsight attention mask, mismatched-candidate conditioning, and query-token alignment) is frozen and its representation and similarity distribution are distilled into a student that encodes queries and candidates independently. The cost is entirely at training time: an extra teacher model, a distillation stage, and the associated data and GPU budget, while inference cost stays at that of a standard single-pass embedder. Failure modes include residual candidate leakage or representation collapse if the teacher's safeguards underperform, and degraded generalization when the distillation data does not match the deployment domain.
rationale: It transfers the benefits of reasoning-style context into a cheap standalone embedder, but realizing that benefit requires running the paper's two-stage training pipeline on the reader's own retrieval workload, which needs validation at small scale.

claims.statement: HEME replaces inference-time intermediate reasoning in multimodal embedding models with a hindsight-distilled student: a teacher trained with access to the paired candidate (via a hindsight attention mask, mismatched-candidate conditioning, and query-token alignment) is frozen and its representation and similarity distribution are distilled into a student that encodes queries and candidates independently. The cost is entirely at training time: an extra teacher model, a distillation stage, and the associated data and GPU budget, while inference cost stays at that of a standard single-pass embedder. Failure modes include residual candidate leakage or representation collapse if the teacher's safeguards underperform, and degraded generalization when the distillation data does not match the deployment domain.

The paper claims HEME matches or exceeds reasoning-driven universal multimodal embedding methods on MMEB-V2 and the agent and text tasks of MMEB-V3 while avoiding their extra inference-time computation; no quantified speedup factor is given in the abstract.
